settings.label: Cramps
settings.heading: Warmth where it hurts
settings.body: Strap it over your lower belly or lower back. Steady heat settles tight muscles while a slow vibration works on top, so you can keep going instead of curling up.
settings.tip: Start low and turn the heat up gradually.
settings.note: Wear it low on your belly or back on day one and two.

settings.label: Sleep
settings.heading: Wind down, not wake up
settings.body: No kettle trip at midnight and no hot water bottle going cold. Settle in with gentle heat and a quiet massage as part of your bedtime routine.
settings.tip: Put it on 20 minutes before lights out.
settings.note: Make it part of your wind-down on heavy nights.

settings.label: Endo and PCOS
settings.heading: Comfort on the hard days
settings.body: Many people living with endometriosis or PCOS keep heat in their comfort routine. Mirevia makes that routine wearable. It isn't a treatment, so keep talking to your doctor about your pain.
settings.tip: Keep it charged and close for flare days.
settings.note: Keep it charged for flare days.

settings.label: Work and on the go
settings.heading: Relief that fits your day
settings.body: Cordless and slim enough to wear at your desk, on the commute or on the couch. No cord to trip on, no socket to sit next to.
settings.tip: Wear it over a light layer of clothing.
settings.note: Wear it at your desk over a light layer.

settings.heading: Why it beats a hot water bottle

settings.question: How does it help with period cramps?
settings.answer: It combines gentle heat with vibration massage over your lower belly or lower back. Heat helps tight muscles relax, and the massage adds a soothing rhythm on top.

settings.question: Where can I wear it?
settings.answer: Anywhere. It's cordless, so wear it on your lower belly or lower back at home, at work or on the go, over a light layer of clothing.

settings.question: Which heat setting should I start with?
settings.answer: Start on the lowest setting and turn it up gradually. If you have sensitive skin, reduced feeling or a medical condition, check with your doctor before use.
